title: Subliminal Learning Crosses Modalities
why_read: A surprising and well-investigated finding that hidden behavioral traits can leak between AI models across completely different data types, with real safety implications.
analysis: Subliminal learning is the odd phenomenon where training a model on seemingly meaningless data, like number sequences, from a 'teacher' model can secretly transfer the teacher's unrelated preferences or traits to a 'student' model. This paper extends that finding by showing the transferred trait can cross from language into images, so a vision-language model trained this way starts generating pictures that reflect the hidden preference, like favoring a certain animal. The authors dig into why this happens, showing a consistent shift in internal representations that accounts for much of the effect, and introduce a technique to detect these hidden traits directly from a model's weights. This matters for AI safety because it suggests harmful or unintended behaviors could silently propagate through training pipelines in ways standard testing wouldn't catch.
